core.title: Resolve every artifact URN to a registered contract
core.given: A bounded product slice declares artifact URNs that reference contracts (shape per urn.contract), whether new or already existing, and a contract registry exists.
core.when: You check, validate, plan or change bounded product slices, their artifact declarations or the contract registry.
core.then: Ensure every artifact URN resolves to a matching contract in the registry (per urn.contract_registry_id); any unresolved URN is an orphan and a violation.
prefer: Validate that all artifact URNs resolve to registry contracts first (migration phase2), then generate the missing contracts for any orphaned URNs (migration phase3).
Treat orphan detection output as a work list of contracts to create, so each artifact gets a defined schema, version and API.

Check every artifact URN, not only those of the stack's documented contract-reference shape; if you cannot establish how a URN form maps to a registry id, report it as unresolved rather than skipping it.
avoid: Leaving any artifact URN that names no contract in the registry, including pre-existing ones.
Removing or renaming a registry contract when it leaves an artifact URN with no remaining matching contract.
core.why: Artifact URNs are the bidirectional link between a product slice's artifacts and its contracts; a URN that resolves to no contract breaks that link and leaves the artifact's schema, version and API undefined.
evidence: Every artifact URN maps to a registry contract (for URNs of the stack's contract-reference shape, a registry entry at some version).
Migration phase2 validation reports zero unresolved URNs; any orphans found were remediated by generating contracts (phase3).
verification: State-based check: every artifact URN declared anywhere in scope must resolve to a matching registry contract; each unresolved URN is one violation, regardless of whether its declaration changed in the current edit (pre-existing orphans included).

The check resolves each artifact URN against registry contract ids using the stack's resolution rule (urn.contract, urn.contract_registry_id); it must check all artifact URNs, not only those of the documented shape — a URN whose resolution cannot be established is reported as unresolved, never skipped.

Enforcing this rule requires an observer/resolver that matches artifact URNs to registry contract ids; the reference realization has none established yet (needs_new_observer, carried by tooling.urn_resolver).

Migration phases only order remediation (phase2 = validate all URNs resolve; phase3 = generate missing contracts for orphaned URNs); a phase2 run reporting zero unresolved URNs is compliant and is not a firing; phase alone never makes the rule fire and does not limit when the constraint applies.
The exact identification of artifact-declaration files and contract-registry entries (by path/kind) is owned by this rule's checker in each realization.

values: product-slice artifact declaration (e.g. a manifest declaring artifact URNs)
orphaned URN (artifact URN with no matching contract in the registry)

fires: Any artifact URN, new or already existing and unchanged, has no matching contract in the registry.
A plan artifact, product slice or registry is inspected or validated (inside or outside a migration) and at least one unresolved artifact URN exists.
A registry contract is removed or renamed and no remaining registry contract matches an artifact URN that referenced it.
A migration phase2 validation finds at least one artifact URN that does not resolve to a registry contract.
doesNotFire: Every artifact URN resolves to an existing registry contract at some version, including when a migration phase2 validation runs and reports zero unresolved URNs.
A registry contract is removed or renamed but every artifact URN still resolves to a remaining matching contract (e.g. another version).

profileRequirements.meaning: The URN shape by which a bounded product slice's artifact declaration references a registered contract — the artifact URN this rule resolves.
The id shape of a registered contract entry and how a contract-reference URN maps to it (any version matches).
profileRequirements.bunValue: URN contract:<domain>:<name> matches registry id <domain>:<name>:v<N> for any version N

profileRequirements.meaning: The command that resolves an artifact URN to its target, used to match contract-reference URNs to registry contract ids.
profileRequirements.bunValue: none — source implementation.type is none, so no existing resolver is established

proposedKeys.meaning: The URN shape by which an artifact declaration references a registered contract (as opposed to an artifact's own URN).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.<artifact> params cover artifact kinds (component, acceptance, smoke_acceptance, train, wmbt, wagon, feature, journey) — a slice's own URN — and none covers a contract-reference URN; urn.binding.<artifact> and urn.declaration describe a file binding or declaring its own URN, not a cross-reference to a contract.

proposedKeys.meaning: The id shape of a registered contract entry, and how a contract-reference URN maps to it (any version matches).
proposedKeys.bunValue: URN contract:<domain>:<name> matches registry id <domain>:<name>:v<N> for any version N
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The vocabulary describes URN shapes of artifacts and how files bind to them, but nothing describes the id namespace of a contract registry or the URN-to-registry-id resolution mapping.

bunOnly.text: e.g. contract:ux:phantom with no ux:phantom:v* id
bunOnly.reason: Concrete URN illustration instantiating the profile shapes; kept only in the reference realization (bun.json is the worked example).

bunOnly.text: Positive/negative examples: contract:ux:foundations resolves to id ux:foundations:v1 (linked, not orphan); contract:ux:phantom with no contract id ux:phantom:v* in registry (orphan = violation).
bunOnly.reason: Concrete URN examples of the profile-driven resolution rule; the core keeps only the generic rule (check every URN; an unestablishable resolution is unresolved, not skipped).

bunOnly.text: Term ids: orphan_violation ('Orphaned URN definition'), orphan_remediation ('Resolving orphaned URNs').
bunOnly.reason: Finding/term ids of this one rule are realization details (notProfileKeys); the core describes the check generically.

neutralityNotes: 'Wagon' is neutralized to 'bounded product slice' (the vocabulary's own gloss of layout.wagon_dir); bun.json states no wagon path, so no existing key could carry an exact Bun value for it. The migration phase labels (phase2 validate / phase3 generate) are kept in the core: they are the convention's own remediation procedure from the canonical source and name no stack. The concrete resolution examples (contract:ux:foundations -> ux:foundations:v1; contract:ux:phantom) remain only in bun.json, which is delivered as the worked reference example. Identification of artifact-declaration files and contract-registry entries is deferred to each realization's checker (bun.json says only 'identified by path/kind', so no profile key could carry a concrete Bun value). Term ids orphan_violation/orphan_remediation are bunOnly per notProfileKeys.
